bands.name: Anterior bundle
bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint to valgus stress through most of flexion-extension range; the functionally most important of the three bundles
bands.function_note: The strongest and most consistently taut bundle -- the one most commonly reconstructed in 'Tommy John' surgery.
bands.source: Morrey BF, An KN (1983) 'Articular and ligamentous contributions to the stability of the elbow joint.' Am J Sports Med 11(5):315-319 -- classic sequential-sectioning cadaveric study establishing the anterior bundle of the ulnar (medial) collateral ligament as the elbow's primary restraint to valgus stress.

bands.name: Posterior bundle
bands.mechanical_role: secondary valgus restraint, most significant in deep flexion
bands.function_note: A fan-shaped, weaker thickening of the posteromedial capsule.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Transverse bundle (Cooper's ligament)
bands.mechanical_role: spans olecranon to coronoid on the same bone; contributes little to elbow stability
bands.function_note: Runs ulna-to-ulna rather than crossing the joint, so unlike the anterior/posterior bundles it cannot meaningfully resist valgus stress across the humeroulnar joint.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The elbow's primary restraint against valgus (medially-opening) stress, of particular clinical importance in overhead-throwing athletes.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Morrey BF, An KN (1983) 'Articular and ligamentous contributions to the stability of the elbow joint.' Am J Sports Med 11(5):315-319 -- classic sequential-sectioning cadaveric study establishing the anterior bundle of the ulnar (medial) collateral ligament as the elbow's primary restraint to valgus stress.

name_common: Radial (lateral) collateral ligament complex of elbow

bands.name: Radial collateral ligament proper

attachments.landmark_b: blends into annular ligament (no direct bony insertion)

bands.function_note: Unlike most collateral ligaments, blends into the annular ligament rather than inserting directly on a second bone -- an anatomical quirk of the radial head's own rotating-collar stabilization.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Lateral ulnar collateral ligament (LUCL)

attachments.landmark_b: supinator crest of ulna, via the annular ligament

bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint against posterolateral rotatory instability (PLRI) of the elbow
bands.function_note: Its disruption is the classic cause of posterolateral rotatory instability, a well-documented distinct clinical entity from simple varus laxity.
bands.source: O'Driscoll SW, Bell DF, Morrey BF (1991) 'Posterolateral rotatory instability of the elbow.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 73(3):440-446 -- original description of posterolateral rotatory instability and the lateral ulnar collateral ligament's role in preventing it.

function: The lateral collateral ligament complex resists varus stress and, via the LUCL specifically, posterolateral rotatory subluxation of the radial head.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

attachments.landmark_b: posterior margin of radial notch (encircling the radial head)

bands.name: Annular ligament
bands.mechanical_role: forms a fibro-osseous ring holding the radial head against the ulna's radial notch, permitting pronation/supination while preventing radial head dislocation
bands.function_note: A true annulus (4/5 fibrous ring + 1/5 the radial notch itself) -- its laxity/tearing in young children (whose radial head is not yet fully developed) is the mechanism of 'nursemaid's elbow' (radial head subluxation).
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: Encircles and stabilizes the radial head against the ulna, the structure that permits pronosupination at the proximal radioulnar joint while preventing radial head dislocation.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
